answer: In a lotus meadow monitoring market, validators could allow one earning key per certified secure chip, rejecting reused chip certificates and revoked devices each epoch. Nonexportable keys stop one chip from backing many aliases; each extra earner requires another genuine device, adding purchase and power costs even in parallel. This assumes honest manufacturers and unclonable chips. Hardware farms remain possible, especially when device prices reach a nadir; honest newcomers also need a compatible device.
